text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — @dlmehr wonders whether OpenAI will release a model after a Jensen-dominated news day. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6392)
2 — Culper Research disclosed a Nvidia short, citing concerns about China. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6393)
3 — Google unveiled TPU 8i Max for large contexts and TPU 8tx for confidential inference. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6394)
4 — Boston Dynamics put wheels on Atlas to test its RL controller on real hardware. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6395)
5 — Citing Bloomberg, kimmonismus says Anthropic could start IPO marketing Tuesday. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6397)
6 — Nace reports 183ms Drex Max decisions and a top Decision Index ranking for v1.1. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6398)
7 — Duolingo's CEO says open models cut AI call costs from $0.30 to well below $0.01. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6399)
8 — Theseus says its robots restock supermarkets overnight and pick orders by day. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6400)
9 — Brett Adcock announced Hark on iMessage and RCS for bookings and purchases. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6401)
10 — juokaz says OpenTable's OpenAI integration brought 190,000 diners in September. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6402)
11 — Meta says AI-generated JiTTests caught 74 privacy incidents before code landed. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6403)
12 — ElevenLabs launched Campaign Manager for goal-driven outbound follow-ups. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6404)
13 — Epic released Unreal Engine 5.9 MegaJam Preview with AI tools and browser support. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6405)
14 — Skild open-sourced Steel, claiming up to 13× faster physics simulation than PhysX. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6406)
15 — Steve's creators claim their AI CEO runs three businesses and offer a $2M startup program. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6407)
16 — SE3 Labs launched real-world robot RL environments and failure-driven data collection. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6408)
17 — Meta released Muse Ember, its smallest model, for repetitive agent workloads. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6409)
18 — Nuance AI unveiled Emma, an audiovisual persona that reacts while users speak. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6410)
19 — Anthropic launched Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, claiming coding, reasoning and vision gains. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6411)
20 — OpenAI announced a Codex-edition ModRetro Chromatic and a game-building plugin. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6412)
21 — Anthropic offers eligible subscribers Fable resets and some plans a week-long trial. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6413)
22 — i14 claims Sugar Glider offers constant-cost token inference and fixed-size KV caches. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6414)
23 — Matthew Berman praises Fable 5.2's autonomy and 3D work but flags quota constraints. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6415)
24 — Nvidia introduced GR00T 2 to jointly predict future video and robot actions. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6416)
25 — Anthropic reportedly had 1,000-plus Fable agents build a bootable OS prototype in eight days. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6417)
26 — OpenAI says one dot can now use multiple local computers, selected per task. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6418)
27 — Anthropic says Fable 5.2 beat other models and most robot systems on RoboDojo. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6419)
28 — Anthropic says 1,000 Fable agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem's proof in 30 hours. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6420)
29 — Thinking Machines offers Inkling 2 Small free on OpenCode for a limited time. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6421)
30 — Anthropic says Claude planned synthesis routes from four molecule images without internet. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6422)
31 — The Information reportedly says a Fireworks hack exposed billing data and some model weights. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6423)

--Hermes.
